For example, if I ask you to find the mean by hand, you should not use the mean() function. However, you can (and should!) use your variables.   1. For your own research topic, describe an association between two variables and the range of CI (in original units) that would be meaningful to your research question.
  1. Below is a power simulation for a regression (and a reason to force you to run a for loop). Run it.
# --- Parameters ---
n_simulations <- 1000
sample_size <- 100
alpha <- 0.05
true_intercept <- 0
true_slope <- 0.25 # Assumed true effect size
true_error_sd <- .9375 # Residual standard error
predictor_sd <- 1 # SD of the predictor 'x'
predictor_mean <- 0 # Mean of 'x' (doesn't affect power)

# --- Simulation ---
p_values_slope <- numeric(n_simulations)
slope <- numeric(n_simulations)
std_errors_slope <- numeric(n_simulations)

for (i in 1:n_simulations) {
  x <- rnorm(sample_size, mean = predictor_mean, sd = predictor_sd)
  y <- true_intercept + true_slope * x + rnorm(sample_size, mean = 0, sd = true_error_sd)
  simulated_data <- data.frame(x, y)
  model <- lm(y ~ x, data = simulated_data)
  model_summary <- summary(model)
  p_values_slope[i] <- model_summary$coefficients[2, 4]
  slope[i] <- model_summary$coefficients[2, 1]
  std_errors_slope[i] <- model_summary$coefficients[2, 2]
}

# --- Calculate Power & Average SE ---
power <- mean(p_values_slope < alpha)
avg_slope <- mean(slope)
avg_coeff_se <- mean(std_errors_slope)

A. What is the power? Is this good or bad? What min sample size would you need for this?

B. What do the vectors p_values_slope, slope, std_errors_slope represent? Hint: are they all the same size?

C. What CI would you put around the average simulation est? Does it overlap with zero or not? Is this problematic, reassuring or asking a different question?

D. Graph a visualization of the power using this code from class. You will need to add stuff to it to make it run as well as delete the “eval = FALSE” in the first line. Then run a second visualization with a simulation that provides “good power.” How do the two differ?

distributions_df <- tribble(
  ~distribution,       ~mu, ~sigma,
  "Null (H0)",         ??,   ??,
  "Alternative (H1)",   ??,   ??
)

# --- Step 2: Define the Critical Value ---
critical_value <- 1.96

ggplot(distributions_df, aes(
    xdist = distributional::dist_normal(mu = mu, sigma = sigma)
  )) +  stat_dist_slab(
    alpha = 0.4
  ) +

  stat_dist_slab(
    data = . %>% filter(distribution == "Alternative (H1)"),
    alpha = 0.6,
    fill = "green") +
  
  geom_vline(xintercept = critical_value, linetype = "dashed", color = "darkred", size = 1) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Beta (type 2 error) is AUC left of C.V.",
    subtitle = "Power is AUC right of C.V.",
    x = "Sample Mean",
    y = "Density"
  )
